claude.label: Claude Code

install.linux:
# Claude Code's own build for this machine, the one Anthropic's installer (claude.ai/install.sh) fetches, checked against its release's manifest.
base=https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases
platform="linux-$(weft_arch)"
[ "$(weft_libc)" = musl ] && platform="$platform-musl"
fetch "$base/latest" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/version"
version=$(cat "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/version")
fetch "$base/$version/manifest.json" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/manifest.json"
fetch "$base/$version/$platform/claude" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/claude"
check_sha256 "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/claude" "$(json_get "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/manifest.json" "j['platforms']['$platform']['checksum']")"
mkdir -p "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin" && chmod +x "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/claude" && mv "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/claude" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin/claude"
rm "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/version" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/manifest.json"
install.macos:
# Claude Code's own build for this machine, the one Anthropic's installer (claude.ai/install.sh) fetches, checked against its release's manifest.
base=https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases
platform="darwin-$(weft_arch)"
fetch "$base/latest" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/version"
version=$(cat "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/version")
fetch "$base/$version/manifest.json" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/manifest.json"
fetch "$base/$version/$platform/claude" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/claude"
check_sha256 "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/claude" "$(json_get "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/manifest.json" "j['platforms']['$platform']['checksum']")"
mkdir -p "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin" && chmod +x "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/claude" && mv "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/claude" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin/claude"
rm "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/version" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/manifest.json"

claude.installHint: When it is missing, weft installs Claude Code (Anthropic's own build, the one its installer fetches) into a folder of its own, shared by every program on the machine. To install it by hand instead: `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash` (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup), then check `claude --version` works.

antigravity.label: Google Antigravity

install.linux:
# Google Antigravity's SDK (google-antigravity on PyPI, with Antigravity's harness in it), in a Python environment of its own.
weft_uv venv -q --python 3.12 "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/venv"
weft_uv pip install -q --python "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/venv/bin/python" google-antigravity==0.1.23
rm -rf "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/.uv-cache"
mkdir -p "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin"
cat > "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin/antigravity-sdk" <<SH
#!/bin/sh
# Runs a Python file on the SDK's environment; -I keeps the caller's Python settings and the file's own folder out of it.
if [ "\$1" = --version ]; then exec "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/venv/bin/python" -I -c 'import importlib.metadata as m; print("google-antigravity", m.version("google-antigravity"))'; fi
exec "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/venv/bin/python" -I "\$@"
SH
chmod +x "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin/antigravity-sdk"
install.macos:
# Google Antigravity's SDK (google-antigravity on PyPI, with Antigravity's harness in it), in a Python environment of its own.
weft_uv venv -q --python 3.12 "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/venv"
weft_uv pip install -q --python "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/venv/bin/python" google-antigravity==0.1.23
rm -rf "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/.uv-cache"
mkdir -p "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin"
cat > "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin/antigravity-sdk" <<SH
#!/bin/sh
# Runs a Python file on the SDK's environment; -I keeps the caller's Python settings and the file's own folder out of it.
if [ "\$1" = --version ]; then exec "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/venv/bin/python" -I -c 'import importlib.metadata as m; print("google-antigravity", m.version("google-antigravity"))'; fi
exec "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/venv/bin/python" -I "\$@"
SH
chmod +x "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin/antigravity-sdk"

antigravity.installHint: weft runs Google Antigravity through its SDK, `google-antigravity` on PyPI, which has to live in a Python environment of its own, so when it is missing weft sets one up (google-antigravity 0.1.23 on a Python 3.12, both through uv) into a folder of its own, shared by every program on the machine. To install it by hand instead: source catalog/agents/server/install_lib.sh in bash and run the script under `antigravity.install.linux` (or `.macos`) in weft's catalog/agents/server/agents.json, with `WEFT_NEED_DIR` the folder to set it up in and `WEFT_NEEDS_ROOT` the folder above it; then put that folder's `bin` on PATH and check `antigravity-sdk --version` works.

hermes.label: Hermes Agent

install.linux:
# Nous Research's installer, with everything it writes kept in the folder: Hermes' own home (its pinned Python, uv and Node, and the environments a launch under any other HERMES_HOME borrows from) holds the checkout, as in its default layout, and HOME, for the commands it publishes in `~/.local/bin` and the shell files it adds that folder to, is a folder of the agent's own.
t="$WEFT_NEED_DIR/.download"
rm -rf "$t" && mkdir -p "$t"
fetch https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh "$t/install.sh"
HOME="$WEFT_NEED_DIR/home" bash "$t/install.sh" --non-interactive --skip-browser --skip-computer-use \
  --hermes-home "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/hermes" --dir "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/hermes/hermes-agent"
rm -rf "$t" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/home/.npm"
# `hermes` with no HERMES_HOME of the caller's runs in the home it was installed in: under another, it borrows that one's environments, which a bare `hermes acp --version` does not set up.
mkdir -p "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin"
cat > "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin/hermes" <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
here=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
HERMES_HOME="${HERMES_HOME:-$here/hermes}" exec "$here/hermes/hermes-agent/.hermes/bin/hermes" "$@"
SH
chmod 755 "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin/hermes"
install.macos:
# Nous Research's installer, with everything it writes kept in the folder: Hermes' own home (its pinned Python, uv and Node, and the environments a launch under any other HERMES_HOME borrows from) holds the checkout, as in its default layout, and HOME, for the commands it publishes in `~/.local/bin` and the shell files it adds that folder to, is a folder of the agent's own.
t="$WEFT_NEED_DIR/.download"
rm -rf "$t" && mkdir -p "$t"
fetch https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh "$t/install.sh"
HOME="$WEFT_NEED_DIR/home" bash "$t/install.sh" --non-interactive --skip-browser --skip-computer-use \
  --hermes-home "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/hermes" --dir "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/hermes/hermes-agent"
rm -rf "$t" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/home/.npm"
# `hermes` with no HERMES_HOME of the caller's runs in the home it was installed in: under another, it borrows that one's environments, which a bare `hermes acp --version` does not set up.
mkdir -p "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin"
cat > "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin/hermes" <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
here=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
HERMES_HOME="${HERMES_HOME:-$here/hermes}" exec "$here/hermes/hermes-agent/.hermes/bin/hermes" "$@"
SH
chmod 755 "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin/hermes"

hermes.installHint: If Hermes Agent is missing, weft installs it into a folder of its own that the whole machine shares, with Hermes' own installer pointed there (`install.sh --non-interactive --skip-browser --skip-computer-use`); the installer needs `git` and `curl`, and the Node it fetches needs libatomic on Linux. To install it yourself instead, run `curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash` (https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/installation), then check `hermes acp --check` prints `Hermes ACP check OK`.

junie.label: Junie

install.linux:
case $(weft_arch) in x64) platform=linux-amd64 ;; arm64) platform=linux-aarch64 ;; esac
cd "$WEFT_NEED_DIR"
fetch https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jetbrains-junie/junie/main/update-info.jsonl releases.jsonl
latest="max((e for e in j if e['platform'] == '$platform'), key=lambda e: [int(n) for n in e['version'].split('.')])"
fetch "$(json_get releases.jsonl "$latest['downloadUrl']")" junie.zip
check_sha256 junie.zip "$(json_get releases.jsonl "$latest['sha256']")"
rm -rf dist && extract junie.zip dist
rm junie.zip releases.jsonl
mkdir -p bin
cat > bin/junie <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
# What Junie's own launcher (~/.local/bin/junie) sets before it starts Junie.
export EJ_RUNNER_PWD="${EJ_RUNNER_PWD:-$(pwd)}"
exec "$(dirname "$0")/../dist/junie" "$@"
SH
chmod +x bin/junie
install.macos:
case $(weft_arch) in x64) platform=macos-amd64 ;; arm64) platform=macos-aarch64 ;; esac
cd "$WEFT_NEED_DIR"
fetch https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jetbrains-junie/junie/main/update-info.jsonl releases.jsonl
latest="max((e for e in j if e['platform'] == '$platform'), key=lambda e: [int(n) for n in e['version'].split('.')])"
fetch "$(json_get releases.jsonl "$latest['downloadUrl']")" junie.zip
check_sha256 junie.zip "$(json_get releases.jsonl "$latest['sha256']")"
rm -rf dist && ditto -x -k junie.zip dist
rm junie.zip releases.jsonl
mkdir -p bin
cat > bin/junie <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
# What Junie's own launcher (~/.local/bin/junie) sets before it starts Junie.
export EJ_RUNNER_PWD="${EJ_RUNNER_PWD:-$(pwd)}"
exec "$(dirname "$0")/../dist/Applications/junie.app/Contents/MacOS/junie" "$@"
SH
chmod +x bin/junie

junie.installHint: When it is missing, weft installs Junie (its release from JetBrains' GitHub) into a folder of its own, shared by every program on the machine. To install it by hand instead: `curl -fsSL https://junie.jetbrains.com/install.sh | bash` (it needs `unzip`; https://junie.jetbrains.com/docs/junie-cli.html), then check `junie --version` works.

kiro.label: Kiro CLI

install.linux:
case $(weft_arch) in x64) arch=x86_64 min=34 ;; arm64) arch=aarch64 min=39 ;; esac
# Kiro's own installer takes its musl build on a musl machine and on a glibc
# older than 2.34 (x86_64) or 2.39 (aarch64).
suffix=
if [ "$(weft_libc)" = musl ] || ! python3 -c "import platform, sys; v = platform.libc_ver()[1].split('.'); sys.exit(not (len(v) > 1 and (int(v[0]), int(v[1])) >= (2, $min)))"; then
    suffix=-musl
fi
name=kirocli-$arch-linux$suffix.tar.gz
channel=https://prod.download.cli.kiro.dev/stable/latest
cd "$WEFT_NEED_DIR"
fetch "$channel/manifest.json" manifest.json
fetch "$channel/$name" kiro.tar.gz
check_sha256 kiro.tar.gz "$(json_get manifest.json "next(p['sha256'] for p in j['packages'] if p['download'].endswith('/$name'))")"
rm -rf kirocli && extract kiro.tar.gz .
rm kiro.tar.gz manifest.json
install.macos:
name=kirocli-universal-darwin.tar.gz
channel=https://prod.download.cli.kiro.dev/stable/latest
cd "$WEFT_NEED_DIR"
fetch "$channel/manifest.json" manifest.json
fetch "$channel/$name" kiro.tar.gz
check_sha256 kiro.tar.gz "$(json_get manifest.json "next(p['sha256'] for p in j['packages'] if p['download'].endswith('/$name'))")"
rm -rf kirocli && extract kiro.tar.gz .
rm kiro.tar.gz manifest.json

kiro.installHint: When it is missing, weft installs Kiro CLI (its release from prod.download.cli.kiro.dev) into a folder of its own, shared by every program on the machine. To install it by hand instead: `curl -fsSL https://cli.kiro.dev/install | bash` (https://kiro.dev/docs/getting-started/installation/), then check `kiro-cli --version` works.

kilo.label: Kilo Code

install.linux:
# Kilo Code CLI's own build for this machine, the one Kilo's installer (kilo.ai/cli/install) picks: the release npm's `latest` names, a `baseline` build on a CPU without AVX2, a `musl` one on a musl Linux.
fetch https://registry.npmjs.org/-/package/@kilocode%2Fcli/dist-tags "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/tags.json"
version=$(json_get "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/tags.json" "j['latest']")
rm "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/tags.json"
target="linux-$(weft_arch)"
[ "$(weft_arch)" = x64 ] && ! grep -qwi avx2 /proc/cpuinfo && target="$target-baseline"
[ "$(weft_libc)" = musl ] && target="$target-musl"

pi.label: Pi

install.linux:
npm_install 24 --ignore-scripts @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
# npm's download cache, which nothing reads once the install is done.
rm -rf "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/.npm"
# ripgrep and fd, which Pi otherwise downloads into each home it runs in on its first search: the builds it picks, put on its PATH.
arch=$(weft_arch)
arch=${arch/x64/x86_64}
arch=${arch/arm64/aarch64}
if [ "$(weft_os)" = linux ]; then target="$arch-unknown-linux-musl"; else target="$arch-apple-darwin"; fi
t="$WEFT_NEED_DIR/.download"
rm -rf "$t" && mkdir -p "$t"
rg=$(github_latest BurntSushi/ripgrep) fd=$(github_latest sharkdp/fd)
url="https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/releases/download/$rg/ripgrep-$rg-$target.tar.gz"
fetch_summed "$url" "$url.sha256" "$t/rg.tar.gz"
fetch "https://github.com/sharkdp/fd/releases/download/$fd/fd-$fd-$target.tar.gz" "$t/fd.tar.gz"
extract "$t/rg.tar.gz" "$t/rg" 1
extract "$t/fd.tar.gz" "$t/fd" 1
mv "$t/rg/rg" "$t/fd/fd" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR/bin/"
rm -rf "$t"

opencode.label: OpenCode

install.linux:
# OpenCode's own build for this machine, as its installer (opencode.ai/v2/install) picks it: the npm package @opencode/cli-<os>-<arch>[-baseline][-musl] holds one program.
os=$(weft_os) arch=$(weft_arch)
[ "$os" = darwin ] && [ "$arch" = x64 ] && [ "$(sysctl -n sysctl.proc_translated 2>/dev/null)" = 1 ] && arch=arm64
target="$os-$arch"
if [ "$arch" = x64 ]; then
  if [ "$os" = linux ]; then grep -qwi avx2 /proc/cpuinfo || target="$target-baseline"
  else [ "$(sysctl -n hw.optional.avx2_0 2>/dev/null)" = 1 ] || target="$target-baseline"; fi
fi
[ "$os" = linux ] && [ "$(weft_libc)" = musl ] && target="$target-musl"
t="$WEFT_NEED_DIR/.download"
rm -rf "$t" && mkdir -p "$t"
fetch https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/npm "$t/latest.json"
version=$(json_get "$t/latest.json" 'j["version"]') package=$(json_get "$t/latest.json" 'j["metadata"]["package"]')
fetch "https://registry.npmjs.org/$package-$target/-/cli-$target-$version.tgz" "$t/opencode.tgz"
extract "$t/opencode.tgz" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR" 1
rm -rf "$t"
install.macos:
# OpenCode's own build for this machine, as its installer (opencode.ai/v2/install) picks it: the npm package @opencode/cli-<os>-<arch>[-baseline][-musl] holds one program.
os=$(weft_os) arch=$(weft_arch)

  else [ "$(sysctl -n hw.optional.avx2_0 2>/dev/null)" = 1 ] || target="$target-baseline"; fi
fi
[ "$os" = linux ] && [ "$(weft_libc)" = musl ] && target="$target-musl"
t="$WEFT_NEED_DIR/.download"
rm -rf "$t" && mkdir -p "$t"
fetch https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/npm "$t/latest.json"
version=$(json_get "$t/latest.json" 'j["version"]') package=$(json_get "$t/latest.json" 'j["metadata"]["package"]')
fetch "https://registry.npmjs.org/$package-$target/-/cli-$target-$version.tgz" "$t/opencode.tgz"
extract "$t/opencode.tgz" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR" 1

qwen.label: Qwen Code

install.linux:
# Qwen Code's standalone build (its own Node inside), from its GitHub release, checked against the release's SHA256SUMS.
os=$(weft_os) arch=$(weft_arch)
if [ "$os" = linux ] && [ "$(weft_libc)" = musl ]; then
  echo "Qwen Code's standalone build needs glibc, and this Linux runs musl" >&2
  exit 1
fi
name="qwen-code-$os-$arch.tar.gz" base=https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/releases/latest/download
t="$WEFT_NEED_DIR/.download"
rm -rf "$t" && mkdir -p "$t"
fetch "$base/$name" "$t/$name"
fetch "$base/SHA256SUMS" "$t/SHA256SUMS"
check_sha256 "$t/$name" "$(awk -v n="$name" '$2 == n { print $1 }' "$t/SHA256SUMS")"
extract "$t/$name" "$WEFT_NEED_DIR" 1
rm -rf "$t"
install.macos:
